CAFETERIA LESSON · CAFETERIA · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Celery — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the number two with the vegetable that makes the most noise — and turns celery into a buildable snack project.

What is this?

Celery grows in tall, ribbed stalks bundled together at the base. It is mostly water, which is why it snaps cleanly, crunches loudly and tastes like cool nothing — a perfect carrier for fills and dips.

What does it mean?

Count the celery sticks is the two-count: one, two. After one and three, two is the middle number children master — and sticks are the clearest two-things picture there is.

What does the child need to know?

The crunch is the lesson. A vegetable a child can hear themselves eat gets eaten again; quiet vegetables need fillings and fanfare.

Why this matters

Celery is the base of ants on a log, the classic build-your-own snack — this lesson rehearses the build before the real one.

What it teaches

Counting two, the fill-and-press motion, and listening for crunch as a food skill.

Words to learn

celerystickstwocrunchribsfill

Say this to your child

“Two sticks! Count them: one, two. Two celery sticks. Listen when we crunch... CRUNCH! Can you hear it? Now let us fill the groove — cheese in the boat, three little ants on top. One, two, three!”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and count the sticks — one, two — then cross two fingers in the air the same way. Snap a raw bean or a crisp cracker near your ear and talk about the sound celery makes. Fill a real celery groove with cream cheese, press three raisins in, and count them: three ants riding two sticks.

Look closer at the picture

Watch the filling finger: pushing spread into a groove takes more wrist control than spreading on flat bread, and wobbles are the exercise.

Ask your child

How many sticks? What sound does celery make? What did we put in the groove? How many ants?

What your child can say or do

Two sticks! / Crunch! / Ants on a log. / More cheese.

Out in the real world

Celery arrives on every veggie platter and in every soup base — the two-stick count and the crunch game ride along to every party tray.

Try it together

Celery orchestra: fill three celery sticks three ways — plain, cream cheese, peanut butter — and take a loud bite of each. Which crunch is biggest? Award the gold medal.

Understanding check

Hold up the celery card and ask how many sticks. Two — said, shown on fingers, or counted aloud — passes.

This lesson pairs with the Celery flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Cafeteria.
